_note: GTA VI money-making methods (story mode), Nov 21, 2026. Read Nov 21 ~05:15-05:40 UTC via WebSearch/WebFetch. Rockstar has published no payout tables, so payouts and unlock points come from named guide sites and are compared side by side. Status per fact: 'agree' = at least two named sources give the same figure or chapter; 'disagree' = named sources give different figures (all shown); 'single' = only one named source states it; 'unknown' = no source states it yet; 'official' = Rockstar itself (Support article or a Rockstar developer quoted by press). Our own wording throughout; no guide prose or lists copied (no per-location lists). 'from' = earliest story stage the method is open (1-4 = chapter, 5 = story finished), or null when no source states it; it drives the page's stage filter. Never add leaked, datamined or rumored figures.

official.text: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told IGN that money matters more in this story than in earlier GTA games, and that in parts of the game you need to make money to move the missions forward. He named boosting and selling cars and robbing places as ways to earn it.
In pre-launch coverage Nelson is also quoted calling making money off-mission "an important part of the game", and saying you learn robbery spots in play and from other characters.
Rockstar Support: the BuckMe account has a limit that rises as the main story progresses. Payments that cannot land because the Checking account is full are processed after the next story upgrade.

Rockstar's first launch update (Nov 23, PS5 and Xbox Series X|S) fixed partners not handing over bags for you to sell to fences, and the game not autosaving correctly. If a robbery bag would not reach a fence before, update the game and try again.

tips.text: Don't farm cash in Chapter 1: PowerPyx says you lose it when the chapter ends.
The story itself pays $120,000 at the end of Chapter 3, per PowerPyx.
Yasmani sells a security van tip for $10,000 once you have robbed two Payday Loans for him.
You can carry up to $20,000 in cash at a time (AlcastHQ; GTABase says $20,000 per character).

coverage.text: Coverage on Nov 23: 15 ways to make money in story mode, each with when it opens and what it pays, compared across eight named guide sites, plus what Rockstar has said. Not yet: per-location lists and any official payout table (Rockstar has not published one).

method.text: Rockstar has not published payouts, so every figure here is what a named guide site reported in the first days after launch, with its date. Where guides give different numbers we show all of them. Payouts can also change with game updates.

independence.text: Several guides publish the same figures (for example $10,000 to $25,000 for jewelry stores). Matching numbers can mean they were checked separately, or that one guide copied another, so "Guides agree" means at least two named sources state it, not that Rockstar confirmed it.

tracker.text: Fencing money also counts toward 100% completion (for example $100,000 of jewelry and $200,000 of vehicles fenced), so the money you make here moves your completion too.
